risks: Valuation veto: engine DCF fair value is NEGATIVE Rs -20.86 — the Rs 112 price embeds growth above the 12% discount rate; 39x FY26 earnings and 6.4x book leave no margin of safety on the engine's numbers

Margin drag into FY27: renovation/tech/GST took 580bps in FY26 and the GST change has a FULL-year impact in FY27 before fading
Low promoter holding 22.3% (screener con) with 43.8% public float — limited insider skin in the game at this valuation
Cyclicality + seasonality: hotels are cyclical; Q1 is seasonally weak (Q1FY27 PAT Rs 45.8cr vs Q4FY26 Rs 116.5cr); occupancy/ARR gains can reverse in a downturn
Demerger execution: Fleur scheme needs NCLT approval within the 6-month observation window; Warburg Pincus Rs 960cr terms could shift consolidated leverage picture
thesis: A clean, well-run hotel turnaround the engine cannot value positively. Every gate passes — zero pledge, conservative accruals (Sloan -0.06), Piotroski 7/9, ETR 20%, no event vetoes — and FY26 was operationally the best year in company history (73.5% occupancy, Rs 6,875 ARR, record PAT). But the frozen DCF (15% fallback margin, 13.6% capex intensity) values the equity at Rs -20.86 against Rs 2,004cr of debt: at Rs 112 the market is pricing sustained growth above the 12% discount rate, i.e. paying in full for the asset-light pivot (managed rooms, Fleur demerger, Warburg capital) before it delevers the balance sheet. Quality is real; the price assumes perfection.
